data.name: Dominica
data.summary: Dominica taxes resident individuals on worldwide income at up to 35% (above XCD 80,000 including the XCD 30,000 allowance), so foreign dividends and interest are taxed, with a unilateral foreign tax credit. There is no capital gains, inheritance, estate or wealth tax. Domestic dividends carry a dividend tax credit that largely removes the tax. Residents who are not ordinarily resident are taxed on foreign income only when received in Dominica. Citizenship by investment from USD 200,000.

regimes.name: Resident
regimes.description: Resident individuals are taxed on worldwide income; no capital gains tax.
regimes.eligibility: Physically present at least 183 days in the year (Deloitte; IRD), or otherwise resident under the Income Tax Act definition.

capital_gains.important_exceptions: Stamp duty on transfers of immovable property: 2.5% paid by the seller and 2% by the buyer (also on sales of shares in companies with more than 50% real property). Additional fees may apply: assurance fund 1%, judicial fee 1%, solicitor's fee up to 2.5% plus 15% VAT. Non-citizens need an alien landholding licence (cost not verified).

capital_gains.rate_basis: No capital gains tax (Deloitte 2026; CBIU). Income Tax Act s.33 taxes 'gains or profits' of a business and a residual category; capital gains of an investor are not charged.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains of a business (e.g. dealing in securities) are business income at up to 35%.

dividends.summary: Dividends from Dominican companies are included in income but carry a tax credit (s.63): full credit where the marginal rate is 30% or less, otherwise 35% of the net dividend, so domestic dividends are effectively untaxed. Foreign dividends are taxed at up to 35% with credit for foreign tax (lesser of foreign tax and Dominica tax).
dividends.important_exceptions: Resident but not ordinarily resident individuals: foreign-source income is taxed only to the extent received in Dominica (s.8(2)).

open_questions: The Income Tax Act copy used is an older consolidation; later amendments to s.63 (dividend credit) not checked.
dividends.rate_basis: Bands after the XCD 30,000 resident allowance: 15% next 20,000, 25% next 30,000, 35% above XCD 80,000 (IRD, from 1 January 2018). Domestic: s.63(2) credit offsets the tax. Foreign: top rate 0.35.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% on dividends to non-residents; no WHT on dividends to residents.
dividends.treaty_network: Only the CARICOM multilateral treaty. No US or EU treaties, so foreign WHT on the portfolio is not reduced; it is creditable unilaterally (ss.64-65).

inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax. A parent transferring property to a child pays 2% stamp duty on its value; assurance fund (1%) and judicial (1%) fees may also apply (Deloitte 2026).

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident: present 183 days or more in the year (Deloitte; IRD); the Act also treats as resident a person present for a continuous period spanning adjacent years. 'Ordinarily resident' individuals are taxed on worldwide income; residents not ordinarily resident only on foreign income received in Dominica.

income.name: Dominica

income_tax.summary: Residents pay 15% on the first XCD 20,000 of taxable income, 25% on the next XCD 30,000 and 35% above, after a XCD 30,000 personal allowance. Employees pay 6.75% social security up to XCD 7,000 a month.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed pay quarterly (within 14 days of quarter end, DSS FAQ). The rate is a percentage of annual insurable earnings and rises 0.25 points a year: 13.50% in 2025, 13.75% for 1 January to 31 December 2026, reaching 15% in 2031 (DSS 'Table of Contribution Rates Payable by Self-employed Persons', Second Schedule of SRO 8 of 2012). The XCD 84,000 cap is the employee ceiling of XCD 7,000 a month (Deloitte); the DSS table does not state a separate self-employed ceiling. Self-employed persons are not covered for employment injury benefits (Expanship).
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income surtax. Resident (183+ days) individuals are taxed on worldwide income, with a foreign tax credit and no capital gains tax. Separate returns only. Brackets apply to taxable income after the XCD 30,000 allowance.

regimes.name: Work In Nature (WIN) visa
regimes.description: Visa of up to 18 months for remote workers earning from clients or employers outside Dominica (fees USD 100 application plus USD 800 individual / USD 1,200 family); local employment is prohibited. The official WIN site states: 'You will not be liable to pay income tax in Dominica. Waiver on income tax will be granted for persons working remotely from Dominica under the WIN Visa', and the visa details page repeats that a waiver on income tax is granted to people working remotely from Dominica. Because the waiver is expressly for people working remotely from Dominica, it covers pay for work done while living there (covers_local_work true). Income tax in the holder's home country remains their responsibility; other income such as dividends is not mentioned.
regimes.duration_note: Up to 18 months from arrival; the official site reportedly does not describe renewal. Fees: USD 100 application + USD 800 single or USD 1,200 family visa fee. Presence over 183 days makes a person a Dominica tax resident.

income.residence_routes: Remote workers of any citizenship can use the WIN visa (up to 18 months, USD 50,000 expected income, USD 100 + USD 800 fees). Employees of a Dominican employer need a work permit (not researched). Citizenship by investment (Economic Diversification Fund from USD 200,000, or approved real estate from USD 200,000) is a separate route cited in data/jurisdictions/DMA.json. US citizens stay taxable in the US on worldwide income; Dominica tax on employment income would be creditable against US tax only to the extent the foreign tax credit rules allow.

succession.name: Dominica
succession.summary: Dominica follows English-derived common law and no forced heirship was found. It has an International Exempt Trust Act (1997). No private foundation law was found and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
succession.foreign_law_note: No source read states Dominica's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate. Common-law rule: movables follow the law of the domicile, land follows local law. Not confirmed in local statute for this jurisdiction.
succession.trust_note: Dominica is not in the HCCH status table. The International Exempt Trust Act (No. 10 of 1997) was amended in 2015 and 2016 (contents not read). No foundation statute was found.
open_questions: No source read confirms Dominica has no forced heirship or family provision law; this rests on its common-law system.
Whether a foundation statute exists was not confirmed.
Contents of the Exempt Trust Act and its amendments not read.
Private foundations: no source found either way; not finding a foundation law is not evidence that there is none.

immigration.name: Dominica
immigration.summary: No free movement for anyone. Dominica has the cheapest Caribbean citizenship route: USD 200,000 donation for a single applicant (Economic Diversification Fund) or USD 200,000 in approved real estate plus a USD 75,000 government fee. The Work in Nature extended stay visa is for remote workers. UK visa-free access ended in July 2023 and the US restricts entry at some level since December 2025.
immigration.naturalisation: Ordinary naturalisation residence period not verified in this research; see open questions.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Dual citizenship is allowed for CBI citizens (not verified against the Citizenship Act this pass).

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment: Economic Diversification Fund (EDF)
routes.summary: A USD 200,000 non-refundable contribution for a single applicant (USD 250,000 for a family of up to four) gives citizenship.
routes.requirements: USD 200,000 single applicant; USD 250,000 main applicant plus up to 3 dependants; USD 25,000 per extra dependant under 18; USD 40,000 per extra dependant 18+. Fees: processing USD 1,000; due diligence USD 7,500 main, USD 4,000 per dependant 16+; naturalisation certificate USD 500; interview USD 1,000 (mandatory for 16+). Applications only through authorised agents (CBI Regulations 2024). Banned: Belarus, Russia, northern Iraq (Kurdistan region); Yemen suspended (circular 15 January 2024); North Korea, Sudan and Iran refused unless applicant has not lived there for 10 years, holds no substantial assets and has not done business there.
routes.investment_options: EDF USD 200,000 (single); approved real estate from USD 200,000 (held 3 years; 5 if resold to another CBI applicant).
routes.fees_note: Processing 1,000 + due diligence 7,500 + certificate 500 + interview 1,000. Enhanced due diligence may cost more.
routes.physical_presence: None stated on the CBIU pages; see open questions.
routes.family: Spouse, children, parents and grandparents who rely on the main applicant count as dependants.
routes.tax_note: Citizenship alone does not end tax residence elsewhere.
